subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw support group-to-main sharing only for explicitly matched bindings, or also expose a global switch that can merge every group conversation?
rationale: Both shapes are technically feasible, but they establish different public configuration and privacy contracts that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Per-binding opt-in only
options.body: Allow only explicitly matched trusted group/channel bindings to share main, preserving isolation everywhere else and minimizing accidental context exposure.

options.title: Global plus binding overrides
options.body: Accept a global default with per-binding exceptions, providing convenience at the cost of a much broader and easier-to-misconfigure trust boundary.

options.title: Keep group isolation
options.body: Reject group-to-main routing and retain separate sessions, directing users toward memory or future named shared-session capabilities instead.

recommendation.title: Per-binding opt-in only
recommendation.body: Allow only explicitly matched trusted group/channel bindings to share main, preserving isolation everywhere else and minimizing accidental context exposure.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing issue discussion and routing history make steipete the strongest available owner for the product and security-boundary choice.
